item.title: Port strike talks resume on the US Gulf Coast
item.description: HOUSTON, Oct 12 (Reuters) – Talks between dockworkers and employers resumed on Monday. Both sides said progress was possible.

item.title: Bloomberg: Shipowners weigh new route options around Africa
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Owners are weighing longer routes as insurance costs climb. Charterers are watching closely.

item.title: Insurers review war-risk cover for the region
item.description: Underwriters are reviewing cover for ships calling in the area. Premiums have moved sharply this month.

item.title: Owners report firmer sentiment in the tanker market
item.dc:creator: Jane Example
item.description: By Jane Example and Sam Writer, London – Owners say sentiment has improved across the tanker market. Average earnings reached $45,000 a day last week. Brokers expect activity to stay brisk into the winter.

item.title: Port operator publishes quarterly volumes
item.dc:creator: Jane Example
item.description: Volumes rose 12% to 3.4m TEU in Q3. Throughput hit 1.1m TEU in September.

item.title: Capesize rates jump 25% in a week
item.dc:creator: Jane Example
item.description: Rates for the largest bulkers rose sharply on strong iron ore demand from China.

item.title: Capesize rates climb on strong Atlantic iron ore demand
item.dc:creator: Jane Example
item.description: Rates for the largest bulkers firmed through the week as Brazilian iron ore cargoes increased. Owners were reluctant to fix forward.
